newsitem.title: CHINA: Albright pushes for market access in China talks.
newsitem.headline: Albright pushes for market access in China talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Monday she told senior Chinese officials of the need to give foreign firms access to China's markets.

The visiting secretary of state, who arrived in Beijing earlier on Monday at the end of a nine-nation tour, told reporters discussions with Chinese officials also touched on Beijing's interest in joining the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
"We spoke generally about the WTO," she said after meetings with President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.
She did not characterise the Chinese response, but said the United States was pleased to see progress on disputes over textiles and intellectual property rights.

China has been seeking to join the WTO, but the United States and other Western countries have been pushing Beijing to allow greater access to its domestic markets and to liberalise its trade practices.
Albright was scheduled to leave Beijing for home on Tuesday.
